styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow grey cart with a stack of folded chairs, about one tile wide and 1.5 tiles tall. The measured facts are borderline. It has 11 distinct colours and a median of 10 per tile, which matches the simple hedge reference (11 and 10). It is well below the stall (40 colours, 17 per tile) and the well (38 colours, 20 per tile), which are the closest references for a multi-part prop. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and none of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted and not a pure black sticker line. By eye, the grey chair stack reads as only about 4 lightness steps. Chair legs, rungs and cart parts are separated mostly by a single mid/dark pair, with little per-part highlight, grain or wear. It looks boxy and thinner than the stall and well, so it falls short of Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material. The outline and absence of flat fills are fine, but a careful artist would not accept it beside the stall and well without calling it thinner and flatter. When in doubt, fail.
